title: Withdrawals failing
summary: Withdrawals began failing at ~17:48 UTC on 15 Oct 2026. payments‑service logs show 44 “bank‑rails call returned an error” messages and a few 502s on /v1/checkout. The only hard dependency for withdrawals is the external bank‑rails HTTPS call (4 s timeout). No internal metrics, deploy records, or config changes are available for the window, and a prior incident (pir:2026‑011) was caused by unannounced bank‑rails maintenance. The evidence points most strongly to an external degradation of bank‑rails.

hypothesis.mechanism: External banking partner experiences degradation (e.g., unannounced maintenance, capacity issue) causing HTTPS calls from payments-service to return errors, which payments-service logs as withdrawal failures.
predictions: Partner status page or API shows elevated error rate/latency at ~17:45‑18:00 UTC.
Retry queue for withdrawals clears once partner recovers.

hypothesis.mechanism: A recent code change or config tweak in payments-service reduced the bank‑rails timeout or made error handling stricter, turning normal latency into failures.
predictions: A deploy or config change timestamped just before 17:45 UTC in change history.
Metrics would show a sudden rise in client‑side timeout errors without partner‑side latency increase.

hypothesis.mechanism: Postgres saturation causes withdrawal transactions to abort before reaching bank‑rails, surfacing as bank‑rails errors.
predictions: Postgres metrics would show CPU/connection saturation at onset.
Log would contain SQL error patterns.

hypothesis.mechanism: Kafka backlog blocks async withdrawal workflow, causing synchronous call to fail.
predictions: Kafka lag metrics would spike at onset.
Withdrawal flow would show async retry failures rather than immediate bank‑rails errors.

facts.statement: payments-service calls bank-rails over HTTPS with a hard criticality and 4000 ms timeout.
payments-service also has hard dependency on postgres-payments (SQL, 2000 ms) and soft dependency on kafka.
Log pattern “withdrawal <id> failed: bank-rails call returned an error” appears 44 times from 17:48:12 to 17:59:37 UTC.
Six “POST /v1/checkout 502” errors occur in the same window.
Log shard for az‑a is unavailable; logs before 17:48 UTC have expired.
Past incident pir:2026-011 (Feb 2026) shows withdrawals failing due to unannounced bank‑rails maintenance; deposits/checkout were unaffected.

assumptions.statement: Withdrawals are served exclusively via the synchronous payments-service → bank‑rails HTTPS call.
assumptions.reason: Dependency graph shows bank‑rails as the only hard external dependency for withdrawals.

assumptions.statement: The log line “bank‑rails call returned an error” faithfully reflects a failure returned by the external service, not a client‑side timeout masqueraded as an error.
assumptions.reason: Error wording matches prior incident where partner returned errors.

assumptions.statement: If a recent deploy/config change altered timeout/retry logic, it would appear in change history (currently unavailable).
assumptions.reason: Change‑history captures deploys, config changes, feature flags, secret rotations, infra work.

assumptions.statement: The 502 on /v1/checkout is a side‑effect of the same downstream failure, not an independent cause.
assumptions.reason: Checkout also reaches payments-service which calls bank‑rails; low volume suggests shared dependency.

assumptions.statement: Database‑level failures would generate distinct SQL‑error log patterns, which are absent.
assumptions.reason: No DB error patterns in logs; only bank‑rails error pattern observed.

assumptions.statement: Kafka is only used for async notifications; the synchronous withdrawal request does not depend on it for success.
assumptions.reason: Dependency graph marks kafka as soft for payments-service; withdrawal path is synchronous HTTPS.

actions.description: Queue failed withdrawals for automatic retry and notify affected customers.
actions.rationale: Restores customer experience while root cause is investigated.

actions.description: Contact banking partner (bank-rails) to confirm any maintenance, outage, or capacity event at ~17:45‑18:00 UTC.
Enable/verify per‑zone logging for payments-service (az-a) and request log retention extension.
actions.rationale: Closes gap G3 for future incidents.

actions.rationale: Resolves gap G2, tests hypothesis H2.

actions.description: Add a circuit‑breaker / fallback for the bank‑rails call (e.g., queue for later retry) and a per‑dependency health dashboard (bank-rails latency, error‑rate).
actions.rationale: Prevents similar silent failures and gives faster visibility.

actions.description: Subscribe to the partner’s maintenance calendar / status API (as done after pir:2026‑011).
actions.rationale: Reduces surprise factor from unannounced partner work.

open_questions: What is the exact onset minute? Logs before 17:48 UTC are missing.
Does the banking partner show any error‑rate or latency spike at the same time?
Was there a silent config change (e.g., timeout reduction) on payments-service that the change‑history service missed?
Why did /v1/checkout return 502 (only 6 occurrences)? Is it a downstream effect of the same bank-rails failure or a separate path?
